events.title: Vincent van Gogh is born
events.description: The Dutch painter was born in Zundert, in the Netherlands. He sold very few works in his lifetime. He went on to create some of the best-known images in art, including The Starry Night and his Sunflowers series.
events.significance: Van Gogh's bold colors and expressive brushwork helped lay the groundwork for modern art. His life story has also shaped how the public thinks about artistic genius.

events.title: The United States agrees to buy Alaska
events.description: Secretary of State William Seward and Russian diplomats signed a treaty. It transferred Alaska to the United States for $7.2 million. Critics mocked the deal as 'Seward's Folly.'
events.significance: The purchase added about 586,000 square miles to the U.S. The land later proved rich in gold, oil, and strategic value.

events.title: Jeopardy! premieres on television
events.description: The quiz show, created by Merv Griffin, aired its first episode on NBC. Contestants were given the answers and had to respond in the form of a question.
events.significance: Jeopardy! became one of the longest-running and most recognizable game shows in American television history.

events.title: President Ronald Reagan is shot in Washington, D.C.
events.description: Reagan was wounded by a gunman outside a Washington hotel, ten weeks into his presidency. He survived emergency surgery and recovered.
events.significance: The attack prompted renewed debate over gun control and presidential security. Reagan's good humor during his recovery also boosted his public standing.
